    BitfieldLayout
    The storage-unit layout of a struct's members, packing consecutive bitfields into shared cells.
    BitfieldLayout.Layout
    The computed layout: one BitfieldLayout.Slot per member (in order), and the total cell count.
    BitfieldLayout.Member
    One struct member's input to the layout: the bit width of its declared base type, and its bitfield width (-1 for an ordinary, non-bitfield member).
    BitfieldLayout.Slot
    Where one member lives: the index of the shared storage cell, the member's bit offset within that cell (0 for ordinary members), its width in bits, and whether it is a bitfield (so the access lowering knows to slice).
    BitfieldSlice
    Read and write a bitfield that lives as a slice of a shared storage-unit cell (see BitfieldLayout).
    ByteUnionSlice
    Read and write a union member that is laid out as consecutive one-byte cells rather than sharing one packed word (see CStruct#unionCellWidth).
